text:
taylor: Hey @people-ops — quick one. My kid is studying in Singapore and just turned 24. They're full-time in a masters program. Had to take an ambulance/ER last week and I paid SGD 820. Can I add them as a student dependent while overseas and submit for reimbursement retro? What exact docs do you need?

maya (Benefits): Hi Taylor 44b Usually students can stay on the plan if they meet the carrier's full-time student rules. We'll need enrollment proof + relationship + ID + the clinic docs for the claim. Send everything to benefits@redwood.com and we'll open a retro case.

rick: Also check whether the Singapore hospital allows direct billing. Many international hospitals will bill the insurer if you provide the policy number and insurer phone. If they won't, you can get reimbursed after we process the retro add.

benefits-bot: Automated: Dependent Enrollment Form -> https://intranet.redwood.com/forms/dependent-enroll. Typical carrier review for retro adds: 4-8 weeks. Internal intake confirmation: 1-2 business days. For urgent bills include "URGENT: Retro Med" in subject.

taylor: Receipt is in simplified Chinese with a hospital stamp and shows AED/ambulance itemized line. I also have a credit card statement showing the charge date (2026-03-04). Is that ok or do I need certified translation?

maya (Benefits): Send original + an English translation. Certified preferred but a notarized translator statement or embassy/legalization translation works. Include the scanned credit card transaction or bank screenshot for proof of payment and a currency conversion (xe.com or bank rate) on the service date.

taylor: For student proof they gave a housing letter and a screenshot of the student portal showing full-time registration. Will the screenshot be accepted?

maya (Benefits): Carrier likes an official enrollment letter on university letterhead that states full-time status and program dates. Portal screenshot is ok as supplemental evidence but include the official letter if possible. Also include student ID, passport page, and visa/entry stamp.

rick: FYI some carriers want an attestation from the university for students studying abroad. If Singapore uni can provide a registrar letter saying the student is enrolled full-time remotely, that helps.

benefits-bot: Tip: for EMERGENCY ambulance claims, mark email subject: "URGENT: Ambulance Reimb - Taylor [lastname]" so intake fast-tracks. We can also produce an internal benefits confirmation letter (1 business day) to show providers while carrier processes.

taylor: Do I get a digital/QR ID card right away after you submit? The hospital asked for an insurer QR code for direct bill attempts.

maya (Benefits): Digital ID/QR is issued by the carrier after they confirm enrollment. For retro requests the card will reflect the approved effective date. We can provide an internal confirmation letter with policy number to try direct billing in the meantime. If you want, I can call the carrier's international line to request an expedited ID delivery once we have the docs.

taylor: Ok sending: passport, birth cert, uni letter, clinic invoice + translation, card statement, and currency screenshot tonight. Anything else?

maya (Benefits): That should do it. Add a short signed note explaining why the dependent wasn't added earlier (retro request reason). If the ambulance ride included procedure codes ask the hospital to include them; if not, a clinical note describing services will help. We'll confirm intake within 24 business hours.

rick: One more: if carrier denies direct billing, we can still file a reimbursement claim tied to the retro enrollment. Not guaranteed but carriers often honor emergency services if retro approved.

taylor: Thanks all 44d I'll email now. Appreciate the quick guidance.
